newsitem.title: INDIA: India says freeing state media beginning September.
newsitem.headline: India says freeing state media beginning September.

text.p: India will free its state-run electronic media from government control by September 15, Information and Broadcasting Minister Jaipal Reddy said on Wednesday.
The government also plans to finalise before the end of 1997 a bill to throw open radio and television broadcasting to private firms, a senior official said.

Reddy told a news conference that Doordarshan television and All India Radio will be governed by an autonomous panel, and will raise most of their revenue through advertisements rather than depending on budgetary support from the government.
"I consider this decision to be momentous and historic. For more than two decades we have been talking about granting autonomy to the government's electronic media," Reddy said.

State-run Doordarshan television has the largest terrestrial network in the world, using more than 800 transmitters. It reaches as many as 300 million people in a nation with an estimated population of 930 million.
India began opening up key sectors under an economic liberalisation programme launched in 1991, but the state still owns radio and television stations.

The Broadcast Bill, expected to be formally moved in parliament for approval later this year, aims to usher in private broadcasters, who can currently only rent time-slots on state television and radio, but not own broadcast stations.
A tentative draft of the bill is being considered by a committee of lawmakers charged with suggesting revisions.

The bill is facing intense lobbying by foreign broadcasters, who face severe restrictions in the bill's current form, and also from domestic newspaper barons irked by the bill's restrictions on cross-ownership of different types of media companies.

"It (the law) was supposed to happen in the monsoon session of parliament but it probably won't happen until the first week of the winter session," a senior Information and Broadcasting official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The winter session of parliament starts in November. The monsoon session started on Wednesday.
